summary: unicode returns the numeric Unicode code point of the first character of its text argument.
documentation: unicode returns the numeric Unicode code point of the first character of its text argument. It examines one character rather than encoding the entire string or returning its byte sequence.
returns: id and codepoint, ordered by id.
caution: SQLite does not define a useful portable result for every non-text or empty input. The exercise explicitly returns NULL for empty or NULL text instead of relying on those cases.
scenarios: Diagnose a leading nonbreaking space in imported text.
Distinguish visually similar leading characters in a staging report.
Inspect the first character of an identifier during an encoding audit.
title: Inspect a leading code point
problem: Return id and CASE WHEN text IS NULL OR text = '' THEN NULL ELSE unicode(text) END AS codepoint from labels, ordered by id.
hint: Guard the missing-character cases before calling unicode.
goal: Use unicode() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
